capacity_gross_kwh.notes: mbusa lists 70.5 kWh battery capacity (2022 EQB 300 page says 70.7, apparently a typo; EQB 350 page of the same year says 70.5).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia lists the EQB battery as 66.5 kWh (no gross/usable label) while mbusa lists 70.5 kWh for the same pack, so 66.5 is taken as the usable figure; the 70.5 gross / 66.5 usable split is widely listed (ev-database, Auto Express) but no page stating it could be opened. The 2022 EQB 300 sheet says 70.7, most likely a typo.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: GUESS: no page found names the cathode of this pack (auto-data and auto-motor-und-sport say only lithium-ion; the EV Database EQB excerpt says no data). nmc is the maker-wide norm (EQS/EQE NCM 811, CLA/GLC NMC) but EQB (MFA2) and G 580 (216-cell 116 kWh pack) are different packs. Owner decision needed.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: EV Database excerpt (seen by the fact-checker; page not opened here, HTTP 429) gives the EQB as 400 V architecture, 367 V nominal. Weak; owner decision needed.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: no page found for this car (EQB / G 580); the 2026 CLA release states navigation-triggered battery pre-heating and Mercedes states no lineup-wide feature for this model year, so this is a guess from the same maker. Manual control unknown.
